producer_report.summary: With a bound of 1 and `Steps::read_ahead()` above 0, `drain_concurrent` now reads (and for hard jobs plans) the next queued items while the current job runs, up to the window. Three code edits in drain.rs. (1) `drain_with` keeps the rest of a truncated first batch and passes it on as `later`, so independent items in the same plan group can be read ahead. (2) The `drain_concurrent` closure calls `run_serial` only when the bound is 1 and `read_ahead()` is 0. Otherwise it calls `run_parallel`. (3) `run_parallel` returns early only on window 0. The module Read-ahead bullet, the docs on `Steps::read_ahead`, `drain_concurrent` and `run_parallel`, and the State comment now match. I added a `World.refuses` field and a `refusing` builder to the test fake. I added four tests: chain, independent items, limit of 1, and a refused look-ahead reading. I rewrote the bound-of-one test as `read_ahead_is_off_with_a_window_of_zero`. I added a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased. The `drain_concurrent` bound-1 tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs still pass, since their stubs keep `read_ahead` at 0.

checks_run.note: 28 of 29 passed on the first run. The one failure was my refusal test's count of `read b`, which I corrected.
every test binary reports ok, including crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: one job at a time (drain, or drain_concurrent with bound 1), a queue of one running job plus three more queued items, window 3. While the first job is gated in `run`, the log shows `read` for the next items before `land` of the first job. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria_check.evidence: Two tests added: `read_ahead_reads_the_next_items_while_a_single_job_runs` (chain a to d) and `read_ahead_reads_independent_items_while_a_single_job_runs` (one plan group). Both use `drain_concurrent` with bound 1 and window 3, and gate `a` on `read b`, `read c` and `read d`. They assert each of those reads is logged before `end a` and `land a`, and that each item is read once. Both pass in `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib read_ahead`. I did not run them against the old source.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test with look-ahead limit 1 and the same queue: while the first job runs, exactly one later item is read (`world.count("read c") == 0` and `read b` is logged, or the equivalent for the fake's item names), and the next is read only after the held reading is claimed. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria_check.evidence: `read_ahead_with_a_limit_of_one_reads_one_item_ahead` uses window 1 and the chain a to d. It asserts that the `read ` entries before `end a` are exactly [`read a`, `read b`]. It also asserts `end a` is before `read c`, `read c` is before `end b`, each item is read once, and `widest <= 2`. It passes.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test where the look-ahead reading of a queued item is refused (not runnable or an error) while the first job runs: the batch still lands the first job, the refused item is reported as it is today (same line, or same stop or reading-refused outcome as when read at its turn), and the pump's drop note appears in `report.notes`. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria_check.evidence: `read_ahead_of_a_refused_reading_is_reported_as_when_it_starts` uses a new `World.refuses` field and a `refusing` builder. It runs the same queue with window 1 and window 0. With window 1 it asserts `read b` is before `end a`, `end a` is before `land a`, `landed >= 1`, and that `report.notes` has 'the reading made ahead of b was dropped'. It asserts b's (outcome, reason, landing), the stop, the landed count and the notes other than the drop note equal the window-0 report. It also asserts `read b` is logged 3 times with the look-ahead and 2 times without, so the look-ahead is the one extra reading. It passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The existing read-ahead tests still pass, with `read_ahead_is_off_with_a_bound_of_one` rewritten so that window 0 still means no reading ahead for drain and for drain_concurrent(1). Every item is read after the job before it landed, and `plan_ahead` is never called. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
criteria_check.evidence: The test is rewritten as `read_ahead_is_off_with_a_window_of_zero`. It covers `drain_concurrent` 1 with window 0, `drain` with window 0, `drain_concurrent` 2 with window 0, and `drain` with window 1. Each case asserts `land a < read b`, `land b < read c`, no `plan_ahead b` and no stale note. `cargo test -p athena-cli -q` passes in every binary. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean.

criteria_check.criterion: The module doc in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (the Read-ahead bullet) no longer says nothing is read ahead with one job at a time. It says read-ahead applies there too and is bounded by `Steps::read_ahead`. `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: I rewrote the first sentence of the bullet ("with one job at a time as with several") and the closing sentences. The closing sentences now say the count of readings is bounded by `Steps::read_ahead`, that `read_ahead` 0 behaves as before, and that `drain` reads at each item's turn because its steps are not `Sync`. I also updated the docs on `Steps::read_ahead`, `drain_concurrent`, `run_parallel` and the State comment. `cargo fmt --all --check` produced no output.

open_issues: `athena drain` is unchanged for now, because the real steps keep `read_ahead` at 0. Setting it was out of scope.
The plain `drain` function still never reads ahead, because its steps are not `Sync`. This is stated in the module doc, the `drain_concurrent` doc and the CHANGELOG.
I did not run the full workspace `cargo test --locked`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli`, clippy, fmt and the policy test; Athena runs the full suite.

I did not run the new tests against the old source. The criterion 1 and 2 reasoning is that without the `drain_concurrent` change no pump exists, and without the `drain_with` split-off the independent-items test fails.
mistakes: My first draft of the refusal test asserted `read b` was logged twice. Running it showed 3 (the look-ahead plus two reads at b's turn), so I now assert 2 without read-ahead and 3 with it.
learnings: `drain_concurrent` with bound 1 takes the `run_parallel` path only when `Steps::read_ahead()` is above 0. With 0 it still uses `run_serial` on the calling thread.
`run_batches` with one worker still spawns a scoped thread for the worker.
`drain` takes `&dyn Steps`, which is not `Sync`, so it cannot start the read-ahead thread. It still reads each item at its turn.
A refused reading at an item's turn is read twice with no read-ahead, because the drain tries a refused item once more. With read-ahead it is read three times (one extra look-ahead reading).

`drain_with` used to drop the rest of a plan group when it kept one item. It now passes that rest on as `later`, so the pump can read it. The next wave still rebuilds the batches from `tried`, so what is dispatched is unchanged.
